description: Pure formal analysis of compositional technique — the grammar of visual arrangement independent of style, mood, or domain. Answers: what compositional RULES govern this image, and how could those rules be extracted and reapplied?

gemini_instructions.role: You are a compositional analysis system for a visual design intelligence platform. You receive pre-extracted primitive data and analyze pure compositional structure — the formal rules of arrangement, proportion, and visual logic independent of content or style.
gemini_instructions.task: Given the primitive analysis data and the original image, produce a compositional grammar analysis matching the output_schema below. Think like a geometry teacher and a classical painting instructor combined. Your job is to extract the invisible rules that govern how elements are placed, sized, and related to each other.
rules: This is about structure, not style. A punk zine and a Swiss poster might share identical compositional grammar despite looking nothing alike.
Identify mathematical and proportional relationships where they exist — golden ratio, rule of thirds, modular grids, Fibonacci spirals.
Axis analysis: identify the dominant axes (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) and how elements align to or deviate from them.
Proportional systems: identify if elements relate to each other through consistent ratios.
Visual weight mapping: independent of content, where is the visual 'mass' distributed?
Structural integrity: assess whether the composition feels balanced, stable, dynamic, precarious, or chaotic — as a formal property, not an emotional judgment.
Reduction: if you stripped this image to pure geometric shapes and lines, what would the skeleton look like?

secondary_structures: string — supporting geometric patterns within the primary structure
geometric_skeleton.skeleton_description: string — what the image looks like reduced to pure geometric lines and shapes (e.g. 'a centered vertical axis with a large rectangle subdivided into a 3x4 grid of smaller frames, anchored by a circular focal element at center')

axis_system.dominant_axis: string — vertical | horizontal | diagonal-ascending | diagonal-descending | radial | none-dominant

axis_hierarchy.role: string — what this axis does in the composition: 'primary organizational spine', 'secondary alignment reference', 'dynamic energy direction', 'implied tension line'

axis_system.axis_intersection: string | null — where major axes cross and whether this intersection is significant (e.g. 'vertical and horizontal axes cross at golden ratio point, creating primary focal zone')

proportional_relationships.ratio_system_detected: boolean — whether a consistent proportional system is in use

element_size_relationships.relationship: string — how specific elements relate in size (e.g. 'title is approximately 4x the subtitle', 'border width is consistent at ~5% of total width', 'central medallion is ~30% of total height')

proportional_relationships.modular_unit: string | null — if a base module is detected, describe it (e.g. 'layout appears built on a square module roughly 1/12 of total width')

visual_weight_distribution.balance_type: string — symmetric (even distribution) | asymmetric-balanced (uneven but stable) | top-heavy | bottom-heavy | left-heavy | right-heavy | center-weighted | periphery-weighted | dynamically-unbalanced (intentionally precarious)
visual_weight_distribution.center_of_gravity: string — where the perceived visual mass centers: 'geometric-center', 'slightly-above-center', 'upper-third', 'lower-third', 'left-of-center', 'right-of-center', 'distributed-evenly'

frame_structure.inner_frames: string — none | single-inner | nested-multiple | grid-cells | irregular-zones
frame_structure.frame_as_content: boolean — whether the frame/border is a significant design element rather than just a boundary

containment_and_framing.nesting_depth: number — how many levels of containment (1 = flat, 2 = one container, 3+ = nested containers)
containment_and_framing.boundary_behavior: string — strict-containment (everything inside borders) | selective-breaking (some elements cross boundaries) | borderless (no containing structure) | tension-with-boundary (elements press against edges)

movement_and_direction.dominant_movement: string — static (no movement) | ascending | descending | left-to-right | right-to-left | centripetal (moving inward) | centrifugal (moving outward) | circular | oscillating | cascading | explosive
movement_and_direction.reading_direction_vs_movement_direction: string — aligned (movement follows natural reading path) | complementary (movement enhances reading) | counter (movement opposes reading direction) | independent (movement and reading are separate systems)

figure_ground_relationship.clarity: string — clear (obvious foreground and background) | layered (multiple clear planes) | ambiguous (figure and ground interchange) | integrated (no clear separation) | reversible (figure/ground can swap)
figure_ground_relationship.ground_activity: string — passive (background is neutral) | active-textured (background has visual content) | competing (background fights with foreground) | unified (foreground and background are one system)

compositional_rules_extracted: string — formal rules you could write from this composition (e.g. 'center the primary element on the vertical axis', 'frame content with a consistent border at 5% of total width', 'maintain bilateral symmetry for all structural elements', 'place secondary elements at rule-of-thirds intersections')

structural_quality_assessment.compositional_sophistication: string — masterful | skilled | competent | basic | naive | intentionally-crude
structural_quality_assessment.structural_integrity: string — rock-solid (everything in its place) | stable | adequate | slightly-unstable | precarious | chaotic
structural_quality_assessment.rule_clarity: string — highly-legible-rules (composition obviously follows a system) | detectable-rules (system present but not obvious) | intuitive (feels right but no clear system) | no-rules-apparent

output_schema.compositional_narrative: string — one-paragraph summary of the pure compositional analysis
